text:
Luke Glendening came to New York on a tryout and earned a one-year deal on Oct. 22, a 37-year-old faceoff and penalty-kill specialist with more than 900 games behind him in Detroit, Dallas, Tampa Bay, New Jersey and Philadelphia. It has not taken. He has played four games for the Rangers, all losses, at about six minutes a night, and his ice time fell to 3:48 in the last one, at Edmonton.

Blue Line Station read the next roster move plainly: "Glenn Gawdin recall signals end of Rangers Luke Glendening experiment." Four games is no sample to judge anyone on, but the trend in his usage says the same thing.

The longer record explains why. Evolving-Hockey had him around replacement level last season, with his teams creating very little offense while he played (bottom 9% of forwards). He is still a useful body on a draw in his own end. The question is whether the Rangers, already without Igor Shesterkin, have room for a specialist.
headline: Glendening's Rangers chance may already be closing
